week01_integrated.ipynb.role: Named features and coordinate selection; conditional class-center calculation

teaching.finding: A foreground count is defined for one 4×4 image block. Flattening in fixed order preserves the block counts; selecting two coordinates can lose distinctions between classes. The optional classifier now implements the mathematics on labeled rows. It derives the center coordinate by minimizing squared deviations, adds squared coordinate differences, and maps the minimum distance back to the class label. In the printed new-image example (4,3), the squared distances are 123.25 and 18.5, yielding digit 1.

application.case: Solve the independent conflicting-projection exercise and then change the class labels, one training observation, and one held-out class separately in a fresh two-coordinate problem.
application.observed: With the single first coordinate of the three printed rows, [0,1] is a conflicting pair. Adding the second coordinate removes it. Equality on the fuller set implies equality on the smaller set. A finite absence of conflicts gives no guarantee for unseen images. In my independently authored hosted test on the new manuscript, the training means were [5,6]. The two centers, sorted by label −3 then 0, were [8,6] and [2,6]. The squared distances for a tied row were [9,9], selecting label −3. Moving one training value flipped a different row from −3 to 0; changing only the validation answer changed three correct to two with all predictions fixed.
